The capital of France is Paris.

Located in the eastern part of the country, this historic city has been the seat of French government since 1790 and remains a major center for culture, industry, and tourism. While Paris is often called the "City of Light" due to its famous illuminated streets at night, it also boasts ancient Roman ruins like the Arc de Triomphe and charming cobblestone squares such as Place de la Concorde. Although the French government officially moved its seat from Versailles to Paris in 1790, many people still associate France with other locations because of that specific historical shift.
